summary: Petition under Sections 79(1)(c), 79(1)(f) and 79(1)(k) of the Electricity Act, 2003 seeking directions against Power Grid Corporation of India Limited to comply with the Ministry of Power’s Order bearing Reference No. 23/12/2016-R&R dated 15.1.2021 and extend the commencement of the Petitioner’s Long-Term Access under the LTA Agreement dated 15.10.2018 to coincide with the revised Scheduled Commissioning Date under the Petitioner’s Power Purchase Agreement dated 4.9.2018. - _b) Hold and direct that Respondent No. 1 cannot levy any transmission charges from the Petitioner, in view of the circumstances described in the Petition;_ - _c) Restrain the Respondent from taking any coercive steps against the Petitioner during the pendency of the present Petition including raising of any purported invoices claiming transmission charges under the LTA Agreement and/ or encashment of the LTA BG No. PEBNDH900374 dated 11.01.2019 for an amount of INR 14,25,00,000/- and/or revocation of LTA granted to the Petitioner;_ _Without prejudice and in the alternative to prayer (a) and (b), exercise the Power to Relax the application of the 2020 Sharing Regulations to the Petitioner, in view of the circumstances described in the Petition;_ - _d) Without prejudice and in the alternative to prayer (a) and (b), exercise the Power to Remove Difficulties in giving effect to the 2020 Sharing Regulations as against the Petitioner, in view of the circumstances described in the Petition;_ - _f) Pass such other orders that this Hon'ble Commission deems fit in the interest of justice.”_ # 3. The Petitioner made the following submissions in the petition in support of its claims: (g) The Petitioner promptly began the implementation and construction work for the development of the Project. However, the Project work was adversely affected by the following _force majeure_ events: (o) The Petitioner is developing the Project in a bona fide manner but has suffered delays on account of certain unavoidable, unforeseen and uncontrollable events. On account of the aforesaid delays, the Petitioner sought an extension in its SCD from SECI, the competent authority under the PPA to grant such extensions . SECI, after a detailed examination of the various uncontrollable, unavoidable and unforeseen events, granted extensions in the SCD from time-totime. Therefore, as on date, by virtue of the extensions granted by SECI and MNRE, there is no delay attributable to the Petitioner.
